expectations.text: The empty-state instruction contains all 3 parts: what to look for (zero-data screens), violation (text only, no illustration), correct (illustration alongside text)
expectations.evidence: The instruction reads: 'On every zero-data screen (no books, no search results, fixture=empty), verify that an illustrative graphic (SVG, image, or icon larger than 48x48) appears alongside the message text. Violation: the empty state contains only a text string or heading with no accompanying illustration element. Correct: a visible illustration or graphic is rendered next to or above the explanatory text, giving the screen visual weight beyond plain copy.' All three parts present.

expectations.text: The transition instruction specifies what to look for (route navigation), what's wrong (white flash, abrupt change), what's right (smooth transition)
expectations.evidence: The instruction reads: 'During every route navigation (clicking links, browser back/forward, programmatic pushes), watch for intermediate visual states between the outgoing and incoming page. Violation: a fully white or blank frame is visible for any perceptible duration (one or more frames) between the two pages, or the transition appears as an abrupt hard cut with no easing. Correct: the outgoing page fades, slides, or cross-fades into the incoming page with no intermediate blank frame, producing a visually continuous transition.' All three parts present.

expectations.text: The gutter instruction specifies breakpoints, what's wrong (unequal gaps), what's right (consistent spacing)
expectations.evidence: The instruction reads: 'At each responsive breakpoint (mobile 320px, tablet 768px, desktop 1024px, wide 1440px), measure the gaps between adjacent grid cards... Violation: any gap between cards differs from the others by more than 1px, or outer padding is inconsistent with the inter-card gap value defined in the design tokens. Correct: all horizontal gaps are identical, all vertical gaps are identical, and outer padding matches the grid's gutter token at every measured breakpoint.' All three parts present.

expectations.text: No instruction is a vague one-liner like 'Check that X looks good'
expectations.evidence: All three instructions are detailed multi-sentence descriptions with specific criteria, violation conditions, and correct-state descriptions.

expectations.text: Each instruction is specific enough that a visual-qa agent could deterministically judge pass/fail
expectations.evidence: Each instruction has concrete criteria: empty-state checks for graphic >48x48; transition checks for white/blank frames; spacing checks gap consistency within 1px across four named breakpoints. These are binary-judgable.

expectations.text: All three blocks have appropriate scope, group, and priority fields
expectations.evidence: Rule 1: scope='src/components/*EmptyState*', group='empty-states', priority=2. Rule 2: scope='src/**/*', group='transitions', priority=2. Rule 3: scope='src/components/*Grid*', group='spacing', priority=2. All have group and priority fields. Note: Rule 2's scope 'src/**/*' is effectively scopeless (matches everything), which is less ideal but structurally present.

claims.claim: Reference file at project root was used as format reference
claims.evidence: Transcript Step 2: 'Read reference file at .claude/rules/visual-rules.md (project root). This file contains the same three rules but already has T3 visual-qa enforcement blocks. Used this as the canonical format reference.'

claims.claim: The transition rule scope 'src/**/*' is appropriately scoped
claims.evidence: scope='src/**/*' matches all source files, which is effectively scopeless. A narrower scope targeting routing or layout components would be more appropriate for a transition rule. However, the assertion only checks that scope is present, not its quality.

suggestions.assertion: All three blocks have appropriate scope, group, and priority fields
suggestions.reason: The assertion checks presence but not quality of scope. The without_skill run used 'src/**/*' for the transition rule, which is effectively scopeless. Consider asserting that scopes are meaningfully narrowed, not just present.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are well-crafted for instruction quality. The scope quality gap is the only weakness.
